name: Universidade de Lisboa
summary: Public university in Lisbon; besides Técnico's GENI (own page), its English bachelor's are four ISEG economics and business degrees.

ib.text: EU citizens apply through the national contest: IB final grade (on a 0–200 scale) 50%, IB exams replacing entrance exams 50%. ISEG's English degrees need Maths AA (SL/HL) or AI HL.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.about: Economic theory with management, maths, law, sociology and history alongside, and electives in the third year. The first year is shared with Management and Finance.
programmes.ib: Maths AA (SL or HL) or AI HL in place of Mathematics A, alone or with a second exam such as English (2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published).

needs.note: Replaces Mathematics A (CNAES table 2026); at least 95 of 200

programmes.selectionNote: National contest: 50% final school grade, 50% entrance exams; at least 100 of 200 overall. 2026 criteria.

programmes.name: Management
programmes.about: Core management subjects (finance, marketing, accounting, HR, operations and information systems) with economics, maths and social sciences, all taught in English.
programmes.ib: Maths AA (SL or HL) or AI HL in place of Mathematics A, alone or with a second exam such as English (2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published).

programmes.name: Finance
programmes.about: Markets, corporate finance, accounting, tax and audit, plus fintech and sustainable finance, affiliated with the CFA Institute. The five best students can do a dual degree at Kozminski University in Poland.

programmes.about: Economics and management built on a strong maths core: analysis, algebra, programming, probability, operational research and econometrics, taught in English.

notes: ULisboa's 'Full Programmes' page also lists humanities and design degrees, but those are taught in Portuguese with some classes in English.
Each English degree is a separate national-contest course from its Portuguese twin, with its own places and cut-off.
Técnico (IST), also part of ULisboa, has its own page here, with its English-taught General Engineering degree.
